events.title: 35th Annual Fiesta on the Hill
events.why: Seven blocks of a genuinely neighborhood street fair — live music, artisan booths and family activities that tourists never find.

events.title: 45th Annual Comedy Day in the Park
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.why: SF's longest-running free outdoor comedy festival, 50+ comics in one five-hour show, with a history of surprise celebrity drop-ins.

events.title: 47th Annual Haight Ashbury Street Fair
events.why: Two music stages, Grateful Dead tributes and dozens of vendors — a fun, low-commitment slice of SF counterculture history for older kids.

events.title: Berkeley Old Time Music Convention (final day)
events.venue: Ashkenaz, The Freight, Berkeley Public Library and other venues
events.why: The 23rd annual convention wraps up with old-time string band music, open jams and dancing across Berkeley venues — the kind of thing only locals track.

events.title: Blues, Brews & BBQ
events.why: Free afternoon of live blues and barbecue in a park — easy, unhurried, and works for all ages.

events.title: Muni Heritage Weekend 2026
events.venue: San Francisco Railway Museum, 77 Steuart St
events.why: Free unlimited rides on vintage streetcars and buses from Muni's historic fleet, plus button-making and scavenger hunts — catnip for a 9-to-14 crowd.

events.title: SF Chinatown Autumn Moon Festival (closing day + Dragon Parade)
events.venue: Grant Avenue between California and Broadway
events.why: Mooncakes, lion dancers and a Dragon Parade at 4:45 pm close out the festival — a classic Bay Area cultural day the kids will remember.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: 'Alice Street' Screening with Malonga Arts
events.venue: James Moore Theater, Oakland Museum of California
events.why: A documentary about a contested Oakland mural paired with live drum and dance performances — a good conversation starter for middle-schoolers.

events.title: Dolly Day 2026
events.why: A free, gloriously odd civic tribute to Dolly Parton with live performances and glam — genuinely once-a-year and impossible to find on a ticketing feed.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA (with Los Tranquilos and a disco dance lesson)
events.venue: Oakland Museum of California, 1000 Oak St
events.why: Free museum-campus block party with live music, an all-vinyl DJ set and a beginner disco lesson the whole family can flub together.

events.title: St. Raymond Pumpkin Festival
events.venue: St. Raymond School, 1100 Santa Cruz Ave
events.why: Walking distance from home: carnival games, bounce houses and a new giant slide and carnival swing, free to enter with wristbands for rides.

events.title: Sunset Night Market: Autumn Moon Festival Edition
events.why: Asian-inspired night market with food stalls, cultural performances and makers — eating your way down a closed street is a great teen evening.

events.title: Visitacion Valley Night Market + Block Party
events.venue: Leland Avenue between Bayshore and Peabody
events.why: An inaugural neighborhood night market with food vendors, street dancing and live music in a corner of SF almost no visitor sees.

events.title: 8th Annual Bay Area Chuseok Korean Harvest Festival
events.venue: Presidio Main Post Lawn, Graham St & Keyes Ave
events.why: Korean harvest-holiday celebration with traditional games, live performances and food vendors on a big open Presidio lawn.

events.title: Alcatraz City Cruises Free Community Day (20th anniversary)
events.why: A free family celebration on the Embarcadero marking 20 years of the NPS partnership — no ticket or RSVP, though it does not include an island tour.

events.title: Corgi Con Bay Area 2026
events.why: Corgi races, Corgi Ninja Warrior and a costume contest — absurd in the best way, and a reliable hit with this age range.

events.title: Free Shakespeare in the Park: 'Antony and Cleopatra'
events.venue: Sue Bierman Park, Washington & Drumm St
events.why: Ninety minutes, no intermission, no tickets required, right by the Ferry Building — a low-risk way to try Shakespeare with teens.

events.title: Hands-On Family Science Day: Stargazing & Planetarium Shows
events.venue: College of San Mateo, 1700 W Hillsdale Blvd
events.why: Free all-day STEM workshops, hourly planetarium shows and solar telescopes, then a NASA scientist talk and rooftop stargazing at night.

events.title: LAMVCF Oktoberfest
events.why: Free neighborhood Oktoberfest with a stein-holding competition, costume contest, square dancing and kids' cornhole and art.

events.title: Maker Faire Bay Area 2026 (20th anniversary)
events.venue: Historic Mare Island Naval Shipyard, 560 Nimitz Ave
events.why: Robots, rockets, Tesla coils and Rube Goldberg machines — the single best paid day out on this list for curious 9-to-14 year olds.

events.title: Oktoberfest Downtown Redwood City
events.why: A Munich-style tent with 2,000 feet of communal benches, German bands and game hosts; the $10 all-ages non-drinker ticket includes a stein.

events.title: Pacific Coast Fog Fest (39th annual)
events.why: Small-town coastal parade at 10 am, three stages of live music, 200+ craft booths and a Family Fun Fest — pure local Americana.

events.title: September Arts & Culture Fest with Live Mural Painting
events.why: Live mural-painting competitions, a poetry open mic and community performances — watching artists work beats another vendor row.

events.title: The Great Glass Pumpkin Patch (31st annual)
events.venue: Palo Alto Art Center, 250 Hamilton Ave
events.why: Ten thousand handblown glass pumpkins spread across the lawn plus live glassblowing demos — a beloved Palo Alto ritual, ten minutes from Menlo Park.

events.title: Third Coast Percussion: 'Time Pieces: The New Classical'
events.why: A Grammy-winning percussion quartet playing fifteen minutes from home — percussion is the most kid-legible way into contemporary classical.

events.title: Tour de Menlo 2026
events.why: The family ride rolls out at 10 am with marked routes, rest stops and lunch, and the Rotary fundraiser sends local seniors to college.

events.title: Walnut Creek Oktoberfest
events.why: Free entry, German bands, Bavarian folk dancers and a 'Kinder Karneval' with giant slides and mini golf; the Chillgarten lounge is 21+ only.

events.title: 23rd Annual Cole Valley Fair
events.why: Ninety-plus vendors, live music, a resident vintage car show and a historical photo exhibit in a tucked-away neighborhood.

events.title: 43rd Annual Folsom Street Fair (ADULTS ONLY)
events.why: The world's largest leather and fetish fair across 13 blocks — a genuine SF institution, but explicitly adults-only and not appropriate to bring the kids to.

events.title: Bodhi Mid-Autumn Festival with Lanterns
events.venue: San Francisco County Fair Building, 9th Ave & Lincoln Way
events.why: Lantern painting, Hanfu try-ons with photo ops, crafts and multicultural performances — hands-on rather than just watching.

events.title: Game Market West: Fall 2026
events.why: 35+ independent designers demoing and selling new tabletop games, with a play zone to try things on the spot — free and perfect for this age group.

events.title: Menlo Park Storytelling Festival opening: Clara Kamunde, 'Afri-Crafty Tales'
events.why: Free kickoff of the 11th annual festival with a Kenyan-born storyteller, right at the home library — check the city site for exact time and age guidance.

events.title: Randall Museum 75th Anniversary Celebration
events.why: A free one-afternoon-only birthday party at SF's hands-on kids' science and nature museum, with one of the best views in the city.

events.title: SF German Day Festival
events.venue: Golden Gate Park Bandshell, 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr
events.why: Free bandshell concert with German food — sausages, döner, pretzels and pastries — and family activities in Golden Gate Park.

events.title: Nexus: SF/Bay Area Black Art Week opening at MoAD
events.venue: Museum of the African Diaspora, 685 Mission St
events.why: MoAD reopens from installation closure with three new exhibitions including Dewey Crumpler's first SF institutional solo show, launching a week of Black art across the Bay.
